result.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], Post#cook then returns raw unsanitized, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders <%= raw post.cooked %>. Content comes from remote RSS (SimpleRSS.parse open(...)) or readability extraction with only CGI.unescapeHTML/scrub applied — no HTML sanitization anywhere in the diff — so scripts/handlers from a malicious feed or source page persist into pages served to browsers. Verified from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a security vulnerability: 1) In poll_feed.rb, content from RSS feeds is processed with only `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` which does not sanitize HTML. 2) In topic_embed.rb's import_remote, ruby-readability extracts content with limited tag filtering but no XSS sanitization. 3) Posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` which bypasses cooking. 4) In post.rb, when cook_method is raw_html, it returns `raw` directly without sanitization. 5) In best.html.erb, `raw post.cooked` outputs the content without escaping. This chain allows malicious script tags or event handlers from external feeds/pages to be stored and rendered directly to users, creating a stored XSS vulnerability.
